cards.text: Banquet number two, friend. Queen Esther has King Xerxes of Persia and Haman, the king's top official, back at her table (Esther 3:1; 5:8). Haman got rushed over here after leading Mordecai through the city square on horseback, and I bet he thinks things can't possibly get any worse (Esther 6:11-14).

cards.question: As they drink their wine on that second day, King Xerxes asks Esther once more what her petition is. He promises it will be fulfilled, even up to half the ___.

cards.text: Esther's been holding this in since the first banquet, friend (Esther 5:7-8). Now she finally says, "If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king…"

cards.question: Queen Esther finally makes her request. What does she ask King Xerxes for?

answers.text: Her life and her people's lives
A palace and servants of her own
A seat on the king's council

cards.text: Then she says why. She and her people have been sold out to destruction, death and annihilation.

cards.question: Esther tells the king that if her people had only been sold as servants, she would have stayed quiet.

cards.text: King Xerxes wants answers: "Who is this, and where is the one who would devise such a scheme?" I bet you could hear a sprinkle drop in that room.

cards.question: King Xerxes wants a name. Who does Queen Esther call the adversary and enemy?
Once Queen Esther names him, Haman stands in ___ before the king and queen.

cards.text: The king gets up from his wine and walks right out. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and even I'm looking at Haman's seat saying, nope, that's a tighter spot.

cards.question: In his ___, King Xerxes leaves his wine and goes out to the palace ___.
Haman stays behind, and he realizes the king is planning a terrible fate for him. What does Haman do?

answers.text: Begs Queen Esther for his life
Slips out through a side door

cards.text: The king walks back in from the garden at the EXACT moment Haman is falling on the couch where Esther is reclining. Of all the seconds in the whole day, friend. THAT one.

cards.question: When King Xerxes sees Haman on Queen Esther's couch, he thinks Haman is trying to hide from him.

cards.text: The king cries out, "Would he actually assault the queen while I am in the palace?" The words are barely out of his mouth before they cover Haman's face.
Then Harbonah, one of the eunuchs attending the king, speaks up. He tells the king there's a gallows fifty cubits high at Haman's house.

cards.question: Harbonah says Haman built that gallows for the man whose report saved the king. Who is that man?
Harbonah has just told King Xerxes about the gallows at Haman's house. The king orders Haman hanged on it.

cards.text: So they hang Haman on the gallows he prepared for Mordecai, and the king's fury subsides. That's where we'll set this batch down for now, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Mordecai first appears in this lesson on card 1 with no description of who he is. Haman, Xerxes and Harbonah each get one.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This card is a flat restatement of Esther 7:4 with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Esther's big reveal is a moment that can hold a reaction or a laugh without muddying the facts.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The true or false statement asks the baker to judge what the king thinks, as if it were a fact. Esther 7:8 records only what the king exclaims, not what he thinks. The statement should be about what he says.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: This card is a plain restatement of Esther 7:9 with no Papa Dorin voice. A eunuch casually mentioning a fifty-cubit gallows is a moment that can carry a real reaction.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The blank completes the king's spoken line "Even up to half the kingdom." That line already appeared in Esther 5:3 and 5:6, in an earlier passage of this story group. The docs say to ask about a repeated line only the first time it appears, and never to have the baker guess the next words of a line. They don't say whether either rule reaches across passages in a story group.
findings.question: When a line already appeared in an earlier passage of the same story group, can a choice card ask about it again? Does a fill in the blank on its last word count as guessing wording the baker hasn't seen?
